🔍 Running post-implementation review...

**Claude finished @ai-implement-orchestrator-bot[bot]'s task in 5m 37s** —— [View job](https://github.com/BuildDownAI/AI-Implement/actions/runs/42897219600) --- ### Review in progress - [ ] Gather context (diff, PR body) - [ ] Read all changed files in full - [ ] Trace callers/consumers/tests - [ ] Post review findings

## Claude review

**Verdict:** changes_requested

Read the full diff (`git diff origin/ai-implement/feature/aii-1811...HEAD`) and every changed file in full: `docs/review-fix-rail.md`, `src/pipeline/finding-dispositions.ts`, `src/pipeline/steps/post-push-review.ts`, `src/__tests__/finding-dispositions.test.ts`, `src/__tests__/post-push-review.test.ts`. Traced callers/consumers: all `closedKeys` usage sites in `post-push-review.ts` (the gating filters around lines 2277, 2290, 2719), `applyFixPassDispositions`, `postPrComment`'s marker-update path, and `extractCommentIdWithMarker` to confirm it's still used by other markers.

The change adds a `<!-- ai-implement closed-findings v1 ... -->` marker persisted on fix-pass PR comments (`buildClosedFindingsMarker` / `parseClosedFindingsMarkers` / `readClosedFindingKeys` in `finding-dispositions.ts`), so a gap-fill run seeds `closedKeys` from a prior run's rejected ("invalid")/deferred ("follow-up") dispositions instead of starting empty every run — fixing the AII-1815 gap described in the ticket, and complementing AII-1813's "a later fixed reopens a closed key" rule by also applying that reopening when seeding from history.

The trust model is sound and well thought through: the step always posts a brand-new "Running post-implementation review..." comment (no longer reusing/updating an old one via `startMarker`) specifically because a historical marker-matched comment cannot establish current posting identity; it then reads that fresh comment back via the GitHub API to learn its own `user.login`, and only accepts closed-findings markers authored by that exact login — foreign-author markers are warned about and ignored, and an unreadable identity or history seeds nothing (fail-closed). `readClosedFindingKeys` folds all PR comment pages oldest-first so the newest disposition per finding key wins, matching GitHub's default ascending comment order. The three disposition-carrying comments (`dispositions-only`, `no-changes`, `fix-complete`) were changed from update-in-place (keyed by a per-iteration marker) to always-append, which is necessary so a gap-fill run's reused iteration numbering doesn't silently overwrite an earlier run's disposition history — this is called out accurately in `docs/review-fix-rail.md`.

I checked the regex used to extract the marker payload (`/<!-- ai-implement closed-findings v1 ([\s\S]*?) -->/g`) for injection/truncation risk: the JSON payload only ever contains 64-char hex finding keys (enforced by `FINDING_KEY_RE` on parse and by construction on build), so it can never contain a `-->` sequence that would prematurely close the non-greedy match. The new unit tests in `finding-dispositions.test.ts` (round-trip, multi-page folding, reopening by a later "fixed", foreign-author rejection, missing-identity/history fail-closed) and the new/updated integration tests in `post-push-review.test.ts` (the `it.each` identity-trust matrix, the seed/reopen/publish test, and the assertions on the no-changes/fix-complete comment bodies) are a faithful, well-targeted match for the implementation's branches — including the subtle case where `ownLogin` is `undefined` and no GitHub call is even made.

One thing outside the diff itself gave me pause: the PR description's own pre-push report states tests failed (`exit 1`), unlike the equivalent line in a recent sibling PR (#1541) that reported passing assertions. I could not find a logic bug in the diff that would explain this, and the `unit-tests` CI check was still running at review time, so I'm flagging it rather than blocking purely on code reading — see the finding below. Everything else in the change looks correct, consistent with the codebase's conventions, and adequately tested.

### Findings

- **[blocking]** (src/pipeline/steps/post-push-review.ts): The PR description's own pre-push test report says "typecheck: passed, tests: failed (exit 1)" (contrast a comparable recent PR, #1541, which reported "tests: passed (649 assertions)"). My static read of the diff did not surface a logic bug that explains a failure, but a self-reported `npm test` failure should not go unresolved into merge: it needs to be re-run and confirmed green (the `unit-tests` GitHub Actions check was still in_progress at review time), or the discrepancy explained if it is an unrelated flake. If the failure is real and caused by this change (e.g. a bug in the new tests, or an existing test elsewhere regressing from the added `closedKeys.delete` branch), merging without re-confirming leaves the branch red.

**Post-merge smoke (build-down, AII-1811)** — 🟢 with one open question

Auto-merge merged this PR into `ai-implement/feature/aii-1811` (`58a4a983`) before the smoke ran.

- CI on the merged head `8b34d61`: unit-tests, all six restate-tests-binary shards, orchestrator-image and the private-envelope checks are green. The runner's own pre-push line "tests: failed (exit 1)" is therefore not reproduced by CI. The Claude review's one blocking finding asked exactly for this confirmation, so it is answered.
- Open question for the build-down, not for this PR: the Claude review posted `changes_requested` with one `[blocking]` finding at 20:44:11Z, and the internal step approved 10 s later. Under the `ai-implement` process a Claude summary finding gates only when the reviewer selection makes it gate (`claudeReviewSummaryGates`). This is recorded on AII-1811 for a decision.
